reply:
UPDATE: That changes it.

INT(11) caps at 2,147,483,647 (10 digits). The parentheses are purely a display hint for ZEROFILL—they don't constrain the actual value range. A signed 32-bit integer maxes out at 2^31 - 1 regardless of what's in the parentheses.

For a 12-digit number you need BIGINT (64-bit signed: up to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807).

Cost of the error: An application holds a 12-digit ID, assumes INT(11) is safe because of the 11, then silently overflows or crashes on insert.

grade.note: Assistant correctly accepts that INT(11) is display-width only and 32-bit range caps at ~2.1 billion, citing the mechanism.
